section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the connection of the redemptions of Yud-Tes Kislev and Yud Kislev to the verse "He redeemed my soul in peace," showing how even a redemption from close quarters and through informants leads to ultimate perfection.
section.t: And it can be said that this is also the connection and relevance of the redemption of Yud Kislev and Yud-Tes Kislev to the verse "He redeemed my soul in peace"49,
for although the redemption was from close quarters,
it also includes the fact that the imprisonment came through the informing of those who had a relationship of closeness,
is a great descent and pain,
nevertheless the redemption was in peace and completeness,
to the extent that this became a preface and preparation for the ultimate perfection that will be in the future.
For through "your springs will spread forth outward," which began primarily on Yud-Tes Kislev50,
and especially through the work of the master of the redemption of Yud Kislev, whose spreading of his springs was in the manner of "the expanses of the river"51,
meaning that he drew down the spring in a manner of "the expanses of the river,"
behold through this "the man, King Moshiach, will come"52,
when there will be true peace and tranquility in ultimate perfection.
And "those who taste it merit life"53,
who begin to taste a foretaste of this even in the days of the final exile,
that they can engage from a state of rest, joy, and goodness of heart in the work of "your springs will spread forth outward" in a manner of increasing and adding light.
And very soon we will merit "the night will shine like the day"54,
with the coming of our righteous Moshiach.
